Company confirmed to be a transportation safety/video surveillance business, not a data center operator. Likely OSM mis-tag.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] AngelTrax is a transportation safety and mobile video surveillance company, not a data center operator. The companys own site describes building mobile video surveillance systems, bus safety cameras, fleet driver behavior analytics, driver coaching tools, and stop-arm safety programs for school buses, commercial fleets, and transit agencies, and mentions hosted, SOC 2 Type II compliant video storage infrastructure supporting those products. The companys Dothan, Alabama address at 119 South Woodburn Drive is described as a business office rather than a data center facility. This registrys facility record naming AngelTrax as an operator of a Dothan, Alabama data center most likely reflects a mis-tagged business headquarters or a small internal server room supporting the companys hosted video services, rather than a purpose-built or third-party data center. This is not verified as an actual data center operation, and this entity is flagged for review as a possible non-data-center classification.

reading.body:
This facility record cannot be read as a data center campus. AngelTrax Mobile Video Surveillance Solutions is a transportation safety and fleet analytics company. Its Dothan address is listed as a business office, not a purpose-built data center. The company does operate SOC 2 Type II compliant video storage infrastructure to support its own hosted services, but this appears to be internal server capacity serving the company's products, not a third-party data center facility.

No IT capacity specifications are published for this location. Without power consumption figures, rack counts, or accelerator inventory from an operator specification page, the campus cannot be evaluated for AI hosting density or workload suitability. The facility record is flagged for human review to determine whether it should remain mapped, be repointed to an actual data center operator, or be removed.

Alabama has 12 mapped data center facilities and 9.5 MW of published capacity across two operators. This record contributes neither MW nor verified compute to the state total and should not be counted in state-level AI infrastructure analysis pending resolution of its operator status.
